expected.note: printed weight 25 (integer, tol = half unit). With k = 1, the fixed-effect model and the placeholder yi = 1, z = yi / sqrt(1/w) so z^2 = w = 1/vi.
tight check vs verifier full-precision value (verification.computed.weight_fixed = 25.0; also statsmodels combine_effects weights_fe)
derived, not printed as a result: Var(FE pooled) = 1/sum(w) = 1/25 for a single study, i.e. the reciprocal of the printed weight
derived, not printed: a single study carries 100% of the weight

note: The source gives only the within-study variance (0.04) and the resulting weight (25); no effect size is printed, so yi = 1 is a placeholder needed to run the engine and is chosen so that z^2 equals the raw weight (the engine exposes only relative weights, not raw 1/vi weights). The random-effects weight 1/(VY + T^2) and DL T^2 = (Q - df)/C appear only as formulas (p. 27) with no numbers, so nothing else is testable from this source.

location: p. 16, figure reproduced under 'PRISMA Flowchart' (source credit: Bialek, Gao, Yao & Feldman 2023, Eur J Soc Psychol 53(1):90-107)
description: PRISMA 2009-style flow-diagram counts (756 identified, 663 excluded at screening, 93 full texts, 78 excluded, 15 qualitative, 13 meta-analysed): flow arithmetic consistency.

rows.study: Bialek et al. 2023 (PRISMA flow, single review)

expected.note: derived, not printed: 15 - 13 (reason not stated in the source)

gap_reason: Not a pooling-engine oracle and no matching engine function: these are review-level PRISMA 2009 flow counts (exact integers, internally consistent per the verifier). The metaelemzes package has no PRISMA flow-count consistency validator (only a PRISMA 2020 checklist in the knowledge base and a Markdown flow template in projekt.py), and tests/source_cases.py has no corresponding call ('prisma_flow' is a placeholder). Activate once a flow validator exists that derives duplicates removed, full texts assessed, qualitative and quantitative inclusions from the box counts and checks that quantitative <= qualitative. No per-reason breakdown of the 78 full-text exclusions is printed, so a 'reasons sum to total' rule cannot be tested from this example.
